record.original_question: Markus's conjecture asks whether a compact orientable affine manifold is complete exactly when it admits a parallel volume form. Is completeness equivalent to the existence of a parallel volume form for compact orientable affine manifolds?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.12. A compact orientable affine manifold is complete if and only if it has parallel volume form.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An affine manifold is a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a flat, torsion-free affine connection $
abla$ on its tangent bundle; equivalently, $M$ admits an atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Such a manifold is called complete if its universal cover is affinely diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^n$ (equivalently, the developing map $\widetilde{M}	o\mathbb{R}^n$ is a diffeomorphism). A parallel volume form on $(M,
abla)$ is a nowhere-vanishing top-degree form $\omega\in\Omega^{n}(M)$ satisfying $
abla\omega = 0$.

Prove or disprove the following: Let $M$ be a compact, orientable affine manifold. Then $M$ is complete if and only if it admits a parallel volume form.
artifact.status_search_result: The Markus conjecture (1962) remains widely open in general. One direction (completeness implies existence of a parallel volume form, in the compact case) is classical, but the converse is established only under additional hypotheses: e.g., Carrière's theorem for Lorentzian holonomy, results of Goldman–Hirsch for solvable holonomy of suitable rank, the convex case in low dimensions (Jo–Kim), and recent work on three-manifolds with centralizing holonomy. In dimension ≥ 3 the full conjecture is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Markus conjecture in convex case
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the Markus conjecture under convexity assumptions; notes the conjecture is open in general and proves it for convex affine manifolds in low dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The Markus conjecture is open in general; partial results exist (convex case, low dimension).

status_evidence.title: Affine three-manifolds with centralizing holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes completeness for compact affine 3-manifolds whose holonomy centralizes a volume-preserving affine transformation, contributing partial progress toward Markus's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress in dimension 3, indicating the conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Autour de la conjecture de L. Markus sur les variétés affines
status_evidence.snippet: Carrière proves the Markus conjecture under the assumption that the holonomy preserves a flat Lorentzian metric.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture proved in special (Lorentzian holonomy) case, indicating it is otherwise open.
